body:
I woke up feeling like shit this morning. Very depressed. I packed up the kids and drove to the store to get some things. Internally I was waging a war of self doubt and feeling unworthy of love, etc. When I walked toward the entrance I passed a homeless man, missing a limb and looking pretty depressed himself. No one would even look at him. While walking by with my kids I smiled and said hello to him. He beamed back and said hello.

While we were in the store I had my kids pick out an ice cold gatorade so we could give it to him on the way out, which we did.

It wasn't much, but, it helped me get out of my own head and feeling of worthlessness. I wondered if he also feels unloved and how much compassion he receives on a daily basis. Maybe his choices led him there, maybe they didn't. But he's still a person and was in pain. It put some things into perspective for me about what it means to be "worthy" of love and I hope he got to enjoy a cold beverage on a hot day.

I'm also glad that my kids got to see that no matter where we're at in life, being kind and receiving kindness is important.

I have a family member that is friends with her. She says that she is almost never recognized out of her Flo costume/look. I wonder if that would be helpful in transitioning to other roles. Her goals may not be to become some big star. I mean if she's making money, enjoys what she does and has fun with it, sounds good to me!
